# Hedgerow — models brief

All models are built by deterministic Python scripts run in headless Blender
5.3 and exported as GLB. Read `tools/blender/kit.py` first: it holds the
helpers and the palette, and its docstring is the contract.

    /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender --background --factory-startup \
        --python fun/hedgerow/tools/blender/build_<set>.py

(run from the repository root of the worktree; scripts locate files relative
to themselves through `kit.ROOT`).

## Look

"Realistic-looking but arcade": a 1944 Normandy village and forest at dusk
in the rain, seen from a third-person camera 2–4 m behind the player.
Real-world scale and proportions, believable construction (stone courses,
window frames and sills, shutters, door frames, ridge tiles, chimneys,
gutters, planks, posts, rivets, straps). Silhouettes matter more than
surface detail because the scene is dark, foggy and wet: chamfer/bevel
edges that catch light, break perfectly straight lines a little (`jitter`,
slight sag on roofs, irregular stone), avoid default-cube looks. Muted,
weathered palette. No text that needs a font. Not cartoonish, not gory.

The game shades every material itself (tiling detail textures, rain
wetness, reflections), keyed by material name. So: **use only palette keys
as material names** (`kit.material(key)`), give every surface a sensible
key, and do not bake images or add textures.

## Conventions (every model)

* Blender space, Z up, metres. The model's **front faces -Y** (front door,
  firing slit, a soldier's face, a gun's muzzle) — that is three.js +Z.
* One exported **mesh object per model** (join parts; several materials per
  object are fine), at the world origin, its **base at z = 0** and centred
  on the footprint (`kit.finalize` does this) unless the model section
  says otherwise. Object name = the node name listed below, exactly.
* UVs box-projected in metres (`kit.uv_box`, done by `finalize`); bark and
  round things may use `kit.uv_cylinder`.
* Vertex colour attribute `Color` on every mesh (`kit.grime` via
  `finalize`, or `kit.flat_color`). Grime darkens towards the base — keep
  strength ~0.3–0.45 for buildings, lower for small props, 0 for weapons.
* **Colliders** (`kit.set_colliders`) — a list of `kit.collider_box`
  (oriented box, yaw only) and `kit.collider_cyl` (vertical cylinder),
  authored in Blender space, the helpers convert to glTF space. They are
  the physics of the game: walls block the player and bullets; a box whose
  top is ≤ 0.45 m above the feet is stepped onto; tops up to 1.3 m can be
  vaulted. Keep them simple and close to the visible geometry (a house =
  a few boxes, a tree = one trunk cylinder). Optional `kind`:
  `'wire'` (blocks movement, not bullets or sight), `'soft'` (blocks
  sight, not movement — bushes).
* **Anchors** (`kit.set_anchors`) — named points (optionally with a yaw)
  the game uses: muzzles, light positions, gunner positions, etc.
* Triangle budgets below are upper bounds; a model that reads well with
  fewer is better.
* Deterministic: fixed seeds, no time.

## Deliverables per set

1. `tools/blender/build_<set>.py` — builds and exports the whole set; accepts
   node names after `--` to build only those (still writes the whole GLB
   if it is cheap, your call).
2. `assets/models/<set>.glb`.
3. Previews: `tools/blender/previews/<set>/<node>.png` (512², `kit.preview`)
   and look at them — iterate until each model reads well. Previews are
   for review only.
4. `tools/blender/notes/<set>.md` — one table: node, size (x × y × z m),
   tris, materials, colliders, anchors; plus anything the game must know.
5. Do **not** edit `kit.py` (others use it concurrently); put extra helpers
   in your own module `tools/blender/<set>_parts.py`. Report kit bugs.
6. Do not commit; do not touch files outside your set.

## Level context

The level is ~140 m wide and ~560 m long (south → north): a sunken lane
between hedgerows, a village of ~14 houses along a main street and a square
with a church, a river (12 m wide, banks ~2.5 m high) with a stone bridge,
a ford and a fallen-tree crossing, then a hilly pine and oak forest with a
trench line, a concrete bunker and a clearing with a flak gun.

Houses: closed (doors shut, windows are dark `glass` panes set back in the

Church anchors: `sniper` (belfry floor, centre, facing -Y), `door`.

## Set `military` → `assets/models/military.glb`

|---|---|---|---|

| `sentry_box` | wooden sentry box with chevron stripes | 1.2 × 1.2 × 2.4 | 500 |

## Set `nature` → `assets/models/nature.glb`

Each tree has a full node and a `_lod` node (same silhouette, far cheaper).

names are the contract):

`root` (at the ground between the feet; whole-body offsets),
`hips`, `spine`, `chest`, `neck`, `head`,
`clavicle_l`, `upperarm_l`, `forearm_l`, `hand_l`,
`clavicle_r`, `upperarm_r`, `forearm_r`, `hand_r`,
`thigh_l`, `shin_l`, `foot_l`, `thigh_r`, `shin_r`, `foot_r`.

(`_l` is the character's left = Blender +X when the character faces -Y.)

Two skinned meshes parented to `rig`, same armature, same proportions:

* `allied` — US infantryman 1944: M1 helmet (round, with chin strap),
  M41 field jacket, wool trousers, canvas leggings over brown boots,
  cartridge belt with pouches, canteen, entrenching tool, small pack;
  colours `cloth_od`, `cloth_od_dark`, `cloth_khaki`, `webbing`,
  `helmet_od`, `leather`, `skin`.
* `axis` — German Heer rifleman 1944: Stahlhelm (the flared coal-scuttle
  silhouette is essential), M40 field-grey tunic with four pockets,
  trousers bloused into tall black jackboots, black belt with Y-straps,
  ammo pouches at the front, bread bag, fluted gas-mask canister on the
  back; `cloth_feldgrau`, `cloth_feldgrau_dark`, `leather_black`,
  `helmet_gray`, `canvas`, `skin`.

1.78 m tall, facing -Y, feet on z = 0, ≤ 6000 tris each. Head with a face
(brow, nose, ears, jaw — believable at 3 m, no need for eyes modelling).
Smooth skin weights near joints, ≤ 4 influences per vertex, normalised.

An empty **`socket_weapon`** parented to bone `hand_r`: a weapon object
placed as its child with an identity transform must sit in the hand, with
the weapon's grip in the palm and its barrel pointing along the forearm
line the way a rifle is held. Verify by rendering the poses with the
`m1_garand` attached.

**Actions** (30 fps; names are the contract; loops must loop seamlessly
— last frame equals the first). Every clip keys all bones. "Rifle" poses
hold a two-handed rifle: right hand at the grip, left hand under the
handguard.

| action | frames | what |
|---|---|---|
| `idle` | 60, loop | standing, rifle at low ready, breathing |
| `walk` | 32, loop | walking forward, rifle low ready |
| `walk_back` | 32, loop | walking backwards |
| `strafe_l`, `strafe_r` | 28, loop | side-stepping left / right, facing forward |
| `run` | 20, loop | running forward, rifle at port arms across the chest |
| `crouch_idle` | 60, loop | crouched (head at ~1.15 m), rifle ready |
| `crouch_walk` | 36, loop | crouched walk forward |
| `aim` | 30, loop | standing, rifle shouldered, sighting **straight ahead (-Y), level**: muzzle at ~1.45 m; minimal sway |
| `crouch_aim` | 30, loop | the same crouched (muzzle ~1.0 m) |
| `reload` | 48 | upper body: rifle down, hand to belt, back (legs neutral) |
| `throw` | 30 | upper body grenade throw (right arm overhand, rifle in left hand) |
| `hit` | 12 | short flinch |
| `death_fwd` | 40 | shot from the front: falls backwards, ends lying on the back |
| `death_back` | 40 | shot from behind: falls forwards, ends face down |
| `death_crumple` | 36 | knees buckle, slumps to the side |

The game plays the legs (`root`, `hips`, `thigh_*`, `shin_*`, `foot_*`)
from a locomotion clip and the upper body (`spine` … `hand_*`) from an
overlay clip (idle/aim/reload/throw), and adds its own aim pitch on
`spine`/`chest`. So the upper body of locomotion clips must also hold the
rifle sensibly, and `aim`'s spine should be roughly upright.

Previews: the two outfits in rest/idle, and `aim`, `run` (mid stride),
`crouch_aim`, `throw` (release), `death_fwd` (last frame) with the rifle on
the socket, from a 3/4 back view at shoulder height (the game's view) and
from the front.

### weapons.glb

Each weapon is one object, **origin at the firing hand's grip**, barrel
along **-Y**, top +Z. Anchors `muzzle` (end of the barrel) and `offhand`
(where the left hand holds it). `gun_wood`, `gun_metal`,
`gun_metal_worn`, `leather` (sling).

| node | what | tris ≤ |
|---|---|---|
| `m1_garand` | M1 Garand rifle, 1.1 m | 1500 |
| `thompson` | M1A1 Thompson SMG with stick magazine | 1500 |
| `kar98k` | Karabiner 98k rifle | 1500 |
| `mp40` | MP 40 SMG, stock folded out | 1500 |
| `mg42` | MG 42 on its bipod, origin at the bipod feet centre (it sits on sandbags), barrel along -Y | 2000 |
| `grenade_us` | Mk 2 "pineapple" grenade, origin at its centre | 200 |
| `grenade_de` | Stielhandgranate 24 (stick grenade), origin at its centre of mass | 150 |

# Hedgerow — models brief

All models are built by deterministic Python scripts run in headless Blender
5.3 and exported as GLB. Read `tools/blender/kit.py` first: it holds the
helpers and the palette, and its docstring is the contract.

    /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender --background --factory-startup \
        --python fun/hedgerow/tools/blender/build_<set>.py

(run from the repository root of the worktree; scripts locate files relative
to themselves through `kit.ROOT`).

## Look

"Realistic-looking but arcade": a 1944 Normandy village and forest at dusk
in the rain, seen from a third-person camera 2–4 m behind the player.
Real-world scale and proportions, believable construction (stone courses,
window frames and sills, shutters, door frames, ridge tiles, chimneys,
gutters, planks, posts, rivets, straps). Silhouettes matter more than
surface detail because the scene is dark, foggy and wet: chamfer/bevel
edges that catch light, break perfectly straight lines a little (`jitter`,
slight sag on roofs, irregular stone), avoid default-cube looks. Muted,
weathered palette. No text that needs a font. Not cartoonish, not gory.

The game shades every material itself (tiling detail textures, rain
wetness, reflections), keyed by material name. So: **use only palette keys
as material names** (`kit.material(key)`), give every surface a sensible
key, and do not bake images or add textures.

## Conventions (every model)

* Blender space, Z up, metres. The model's **front faces -Y** (front door,
  firing slit, a soldier's face, a gun's muzzle) — that is three.js +Z.
* One exported **mesh object per model** (join parts; several materials per
  object are fine), at the world origin, its **base at z = 0** and centred
  on the footprint (`kit.finalize` does this) unless the model section
  says otherwise. Object name = the node name listed below, exactly.
* UVs box-projected in metres (`kit.uv_box`, done by `finalize`); bark and
  round things may use `kit.uv_cylinder`.
* Vertex colour attribute `Color` on every mesh (`kit.grime` via
  `finalize`, or `kit.flat_color`). Grime darkens towards the base — keep
  strength ~0.3–0.45 for buildings, lower for small props, 0 for weapons.
* **Colliders** (`kit.set_colliders`) — a list of `kit.collider_box`
  (oriented box, yaw only) and `kit.collider_cyl` (vertical cylinder),
  authored in Blender space, the helpers convert to glTF space. They are
  the physics of the game: walls block the player and bullets; a box whose
  top is ≤ 0.45 m above the feet is stepped onto; tops up to 1.3 m can be
  vaulted. Keep them simple and close to the visible geometry (a house =
  a few boxes, a tree = one trunk cylinder). Optional `kind`:
  `'wire'` (blocks movement, not bullets or sight), `'soft'` (blocks
  sight, not movement — bushes).
* **Anchors** (`kit.set_anchors`) — named points (optionally with a yaw)
  the game uses: muzzles, light positions, gunner positions, etc.
* Triangle budgets below are upper bounds; a model that reads well with
  fewer is better.
* Deterministic: fixed seeds, no time.

## Deliverables per set

1. `tools/blender/build_<set>.py` — builds and exports the whole set; accepts
   node names after `--` to build only those (still writes the whole GLB
   if it is cheap, your call).
2. `assets/models/<set>.glb`.
3. Previews: `tools/blender/previews/<set>/<node>.png` (512², `kit.preview`)
   and look at them — iterate until each model reads well. Previews are
   for review only.
4. `tools/blender/notes/<set>.md` — one table: node, size (x × y × z m),
   tris, materials, colliders, anchors; plus anything the game must know.
5. Do **not** edit `kit.py` (others use it concurrently); put extra helpers
   in your own module `tools/blender/<set>_parts.py`. Report kit bugs.
6. Do not commit; do not touch files outside your set.

## Level context

The level is ~140 m wide and ~560 m long (south → north): a sunken lane
between hedgerows, a village of ~14 houses along a main street and a square
with a church, a river (12 m wide, banks ~2.5 m high) with a stone bridge,
a ford and a fallen-tree crossing, then a hilly pine and oak forest with a
trench line, a concrete bunker and a clearing with a flak gun.

broadleaves, so silhouettes read in fog. Trunks with root flare.

`clavicle_l`, `upperarm_l`, `forearm_l`, `hand_l`,
`clavicle_r`, `upperarm_r`, `forearm_r`, `hand_r`,
`thigh_l`, `shin_l`, `foot_l`, `thigh_r`, `shin_r`, `foot_r`.

  `helmet_od`, `leather`, `skin`.
* `axis` — German Heer rifleman 1944: Stahlhelm (the flared coal-scuttle
  silhouette is essential), M40 field-grey tunic with four pockets,
  trousers bloused into tall black jackboots, black belt with Y-straps,
  ammo pouches at the front, bread bag, fluted gas-mask canister on the
  back; `cloth_feldgrau`, `cloth_feldgrau_dark`, `leather_black`,
  `helmet_gray`, `canvas`, `skin`.

An empty **`socket_weapon`** parented to bone `hand_r`: a weapon object
placed as its child with an identity transform must sit in the hand, with
the weapon's grip in the palm and its barrel pointing along the forearm
line the way a rifle is held. Verify by rendering the poses with the
`m1_garand` attached.

**Actions** (30 fps; names are the contract; loops must loop seamlessly
— last frame equals the first). Every clip keys all bones. "Rifle" poses
hold a two-handed rifle: right hand at the grip, left hand under the
handguard.

| action | frames | what |
|---|---|---|
| `idle` | 60, loop | standing, rifle at low ready, breathing |
| `walk` | 32, loop | walking forward, rifle low ready |
| `walk_back` | 32, loop | walking backwards |
| `strafe_l`, `strafe_r` | 28, loop | side-stepping left / right, facing forward |
| `run` | 20, loop | running forward, rifle at port arms across the chest |
| `crouch_idle` | 60, loop | crouched (head at ~1.15 m), rifle ready |
| `crouch_walk` | 36, loop | crouched walk forward |
| `aim` | 30, loop | standing, rifle shouldered, sighting **straight ahead (-Y), level**: muzzle at ~1.45 m; minimal sway |
| `crouch_aim` | 30, loop | the same crouched (muzzle ~1.0 m) |
| `reload` | 48 | upper body: rifle down, hand to belt, back (legs neutral) |
| `throw` | 30 | upper body grenade throw (right arm overhand, rifle in left hand) |
| `hit` | 12 | short flinch |
| `death_fwd` | 40 | shot from the front: falls backwards, ends lying on the back |
| `death_back` | 40 | shot from behind: falls forwards, ends face down |
| `death_crumple` | 36 | knees buckle, slumps to the side |

The game plays the legs (`root`, `hips`, `thigh_*`, `shin_*`, `foot_*`)

the socket, from a 3/4 back view at shoulder height (the game's view) and
from the front.

Each weapon is one object, **origin at the firing hand's grip**, barrel
along **-Y**, top +Z. Anchors `muzzle` (end of the barrel) and `offhand`
(where the left hand holds it). `gun_wood`, `gun_metal`,
`gun_metal_worn`, `leather` (sling).

| `thompson` | M1A1 Thompson SMG with stick magazine | 1500 |
| `kar98k` | Karabiner 98k rifle | 1500 |
| `mp40` | MP 40 SMG, stock folded out | 1500 |
| `mg42` | MG 42 on its bipod, origin at the bipod feet centre (it sits on sandbags), barrel along -Y | 2000 |
| `grenade_us` | Mk 2 "pineapple" grenade, origin at its centre | 200 |
| `grenade_de` | Stielhandgranate 24 (stick grenade), origin at its centre of mass | 150 |

Iterate with previews (`kit.preview` or your own Cycles camera; 512², ~16 samples): render the deliverable previews listed in the brief into `fun/hedgerow/tools/blender/previews/soldier/` and actually look at them with the Read tool; fix what looks wrong (hands not on the rifle, clipping, broken weights, floating feet) before finishing. Keep the build deterministic and reasonably fast (< ~5 min).

Deliver: `fun/hedgerow/tools/blender/build_soldier.py` (+ parts module), the two GLBs, previews, and `fun/hedgerow/tools/blender/notes/soldier.md` (node table, bone list with rest head positions in glTF space, the actions with durations, the socket's transform, weapon anchors in glTF space, tris, sizes). Final message: a short report with the exact node/bone/action names exported, file sizes, anything the game engine must know (e.g. bone axis conventions, whether the aim pose muzzle direction matches -Y/three +Z), and any kit.py bugs found.

"""Hedgerow — tileable detail textures.

    python3 fun/hedgerow/tools/textures.py            # all
    python3 fun/hedgerow/tools/textures.py stone mud  # some

Writes `assets/textures/<name>.webp` (512², tileable, lossy WebP).

Two kinds:

* detail textures for models (stone, plaster, brick, tile, slate, planks,
  bark, fabric, concrete, metal, rock, foliage): RGB = tangent-space normal,
  A = albedo detail (0.5 = the palette colour, darker below, lighter above).
  The game tints them with each material's palette colour.
* ground textures for the terrain (mud, grass, forest, cobble): RGB = albedo
  (sRGB), A = height; their normals come from `<name>_n.webp` (RGB normal,
  A = roughness).

Everything is built from periodic pieces (spectral noise from filtered white
noise, cell noise with wrap-around distances, np.roll), so every texture
tiles. Deterministic: fixed seeds.
"""
import os, sys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
OUT = os.path.join(HERE, '..', 'assets', 'textures')
N = 512


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# periodic building blocks

def spectral(n, beta, seed, lo=1.0, hi=None, aniso=(1.0, 1.0)):
    """Tileable fractal noise: white noise filtered by 1/f^beta. aniso
    stretches the spectrum (x, y) for streaky noise. Returns 0..1."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    w = rng.standard_normal((n, n))
    F = np.fft.fft2(w)
    fy = np.fft.fftfreq(n)[:, None] * n * aniso[1]
    fx = np.fft.fftfreq(n)[None, :] * n * aniso[0]
    f = np.sqrt(fx * fx + fy * fy)
    f[0, 0] = 1.0
    amp = 1.0 / np.power(f, beta)
    amp[f < lo] = 0.0
    if hi is not None:
        amp *= np.exp(-(f / hi) ** 2)
    out = np.real(np.fft.ifft2(F * amp))
    out -= out.min()
    out /= max(out.max(), 1e-9)
    return out


def cells(n, count, seed, stretch=(1.0, 1.0), jitter=1.0, grid=None):
    """Periodic Worley noise. Returns (F1, F2, id) with distances in pixels.
    `grid` = (gx, gy) places one point per grid cell (jittered) instead of
    uniformly random points."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    if grid:
        gx, gy = grid
        xs, ys = np.meshgrid(np.arange(gx), np.arange(gy))
        px = (xs.ravel() + 0.5 + (rng.random(gx * gy) - 0.5) * jitter) * n / gx
        py = (ys.ravel() + 0.5 + (rng.random(gx * gy) - 0.5) * jitter) * n / gy
    else:
        px = rng.random(count) * n
        py = rng.random(count) * n
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:n, 0:n].astype(np.float32)
    f1 = np.full((n, n), 1e9, np.float32)
    f2 = np.full((n, n), 1e9, np.float32)
    ident = np.zeros((n, n), np.int32)
    sx, sy = stretch
    for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(px, py)):
        dx = np.abs(xx - x)
        dx = np.minimum(dx, n - dx) / sx
        dy = np.abs(yy - y)
        dy = np.minimum(dy, n - dy) / sy
        d = np.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)
        closer = d < f1
        f2 = np.where(closer, f1, np.minimum(f2, d))
        ident = np.where(closer, i, ident)
        f1 = np.where(closer, d, f1)
    return f1, f2, ident


def smoothstep(a, b, x):
    t = np.clip((x - a) / (b - a), 0.0, 1.0)
    return t * t * (3 - 2 * t)


def blur(img, r):
    """Periodic box-ish blur (three box passes ~ gaussian)."""
    out = img.astype(np.float32)
    for _ in range(3):
        acc = np.zeros_like(out)
        for d in range(-r, r + 1):
            acc += np.roll(out, d, axis=1)
        out = acc / (2 * r + 1)
        acc = np.zeros_like(out)
        for d in range(-r, r + 1):
            acc += np.roll(out, d, axis=0)
        out = acc / (2 * r + 1)
    return out


def normal_from_height(h, strength):
    """Tangent-space normal (OpenGL convention, +Y up in the image = -row)."""
    dx = (np.roll(h, -1, axis=1) - np.roll(h, 1, axis=1)) * 0.5
    dy = (np.roll(h, 1, axis=0) - np.roll(h, -1, axis=0)) * 0.5
    nx = -dx * strength
    ny = -dy * strength
    nz = np.ones_like(h)
    l = np.sqrt(nx * nx + ny * ny + nz * nz)
    return np.stack([nx / l, ny / l, nz / l], axis=-1)


def per_cell(ident, seed, count=None):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    vals = rng.random(int(ident.max()) + 1)
    return vals[ident]


def rect_layout(n, rows, cols, seed, offset_rows=True, jitter=0.0, widths=None):
    """Row/column brick-like layout: returns (u, v) within each cell (0..1),
    cell id, and distance to the cell edge in pixels (min of x and y)."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:n, 0:n].astype(np.float32)
    rh = n / rows
    row = np.floor(yy / rh).astype(np.int32)
    v = (yy - row * rh) / rh
    shift = np.where(row % 2 == 1, 0.5, 0.0) if offset_rows else 0.0
    row_jit = rng.random(rows) * jitter
    cw = n / cols
    xs = (xx / cw + shift + row_jit[row]) % cols
    col = np.floor(xs).astype(np.int32)
    u = xs - col
    ident = row * cols + col
    ex = np.minimum(u, 1 - u) * cw
    ey = np.minimum(v, 1 - v) * rh
    return u, v, ident, np.minimum(ex, ey), ex, ey


def pack_detail(name, height, albedo, strength):
    """RGB = normal from height, A = albedo detail (0..1, 0.5 neutral)."""
    nrm = normal_from_height(height, strength)
    rgb = ((nrm * 0.5 + 0.5) * 255).clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    a = (np.clip(albedo, 0, 1) * 255).astype(np.uint8)
    img = np.dstack([rgb, a])
    save(name, img)


def pack_ground(name, albedo_rgb, height, rough, strength):
    rgb = (np.clip(albedo_rgb, 0, 1) ** (1 / 2.2) * 255).astype(np.uint8)
    a = (np.clip(height, 0, 1) * 255).astype(np.uint8)
    save(name, np.dstack([rgb, a]))
    nrm = normal_from_height(height, strength)
    nrgb = ((nrm * 0.5 + 0.5) * 255).clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    save(name + '_n', np.dstack([nrgb, (np.clip(rough, 0, 1) * 255).astype(np.uint8)]))


def save(name, img):
    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(OUT, name + '.webp')
    Image.fromarray(img, 'RGBA').save(path, 'WEBP', quality=88, method=6, exact=True)
    print(f'{name:10s} {os.path.getsize(path) // 1024:4d} KB')


def lin(hexcode):
    c = np.array([int(hexcode[i:i + 2], 16) / 255 for i in (1, 3, 5)])
    return np.where(c <= 0.04045, c / 12.92, ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4)


def mix(a, b, t):
    t = t[..., None] if np.ndim(t) == 2 else t
    return a * (1 - t) + b * t


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# model detail textures (tile = see materials.js for metres per tile)

def stone():
    """Rubble masonry, ~2 m tile: irregular stones in rough courses, mortar."""
    f1, f2, ident = cells(N, 0, 11, stretch=(1.35, 1.0), jitter=0.9, grid=(9, 12))
    edge = f2 - f1
    mortar = 1 - smoothstep(1.5, 6.0, edge)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 12)
    bulge = smoothstep(0.0, 14.0, edge) ** 0.6
    fine = spectral(N, 1.6, 13, lo=4)
    grain = spectral(N, 1.0, 14, lo=40)
    h = bulge * (0.7 + 0.3 * rnd) + 0.25 * fine + 0.08 * grain
    h = h * (1 - 0.8 * mortar)
    alb = 0.42 + 0.22 * rnd + 0.18 * (fine - 0.5) + 0.08 * (grain - 0.5)
    alb = alb * (1 - 0.35 * mortar) + 0.08 * mortar
    pack_detail('stone', h, alb, 5.0)


def plaster():
    """Lime plaster, ~2 m tile: blotches, trowel marks, hairline cracks,
    a few patches fallen off."""
    low = spectral(N, 2.2, 21, lo=1)
    mid = spectral(N, 1.5, 22, lo=6)
    fine = spectral(N, 0.9, 23, lo=60)
    f1, f2, _ = cells(N, 0, 24, grid=(5, 5), jitter=1.0)
    crack = 1 - smoothstep(0.0, 1.2, f2 - f1)
    crack *= smoothstep(0.55, 0.75, spectral(N, 2.0, 25, lo=2))
    patch = smoothstep(0.78, 0.82, spectral(N, 2.4, 26, lo=2))
    h = 0.5 + 0.25 * (mid - 0.5) + 0.12 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.5 * crack - 0.35 * patch
    alb = 0.5 + 0.28 * (low - 0.5) + 0.1 * (mid - 0.5) + 0.06 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.3 * crack - 0.18 * patch
    pack_detail('plaster', h, alb, 3.0)


def brick():
    """Brick, 1 m tile: 4 bricks across, 14 courses."""
    u, v, ident, edge, ex, ey = rect_layout(N, 14, 4, 31)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 32)
    mortar = 1 - smoothstep(1.0, 3.0, edge)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.3, 33, lo=8)
    chips = smoothstep(0.72, 0.8, spectral(N, 1.8, 34, lo=4))
    h = (smoothstep(0, 5, edge) * 0.8 + 0.2 * fine) * (1 - mortar) - 0.25 * chips
    alb = 0.38 + 0.3 * rnd + 0.12 * (fine - 0.5)
    alb = alb * (1 - mortar) + 0.62 * mortar
    pack_detail('brick', h, alb, 4.0)


def tile():
    """Barrel (Roman) roof tiles, 2 m tile: 8 channels across, 10 courses."""
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:N, 0:N].astype(np.float32)
    rows, cols = 10, 8
    rh, cw = N / rows, N / cols
    row = np.floor(yy / rh)
    v = (yy - row * rh) / rh
    shift = np.where(row % 2 == 1, 0.5, 0.0)
    xs = xx / cw + shift
    col = np.floor(xs)
    u = xs - col
    ident = (row * cols + (col % cols)).astype(np.int32)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 41)
    curve = np.sin(u * np.pi) ** 0.7
    # each course overlaps the one below: the lower edge is raised, a shadow above it
    overlap = smoothstep(0.0, 0.25, v) * (1 - 0.6 * smoothstep(0.85, 1.0, v))
    fine = spectral(N, 1.4, 42, lo=8)
    h = 0.55 * curve + 0.35 * (1 - v) + 0.1 * fine
    alb = 0.45 + 0.25 * rnd + 0.12 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.25 * (1 - overlap) - 0.15 * (1 - curve)
    lichen = smoothstep(0.7, 0.8, spectral(N, 1.8, 43, lo=3))
    alb = alb * (1 - 0.3 * lichen)
    pack_detail('tile', h, alb, 6.0)


def slate():
    """Slate roof, 2 m tile: 9 courses of staggered rectangular slates."""
    u, v, ident, edge, ex, ey = rect_layout(N, 9, 7, 51, jitter=0.15)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 52)
    gap = 1 - smoothstep(0.5, 2.0, ex)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.2, 53, lo=10, aniso=(1.0, 0.4))
    h = (1 - v) * 0.6 + 0.15 * fine - 0.4 * gap
    alb = 0.45 + 0.18 * rnd + 0.1 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.3 * smoothstep(0.85, 1.0, v) - 0.25 * gap
    pack_detail('slate', h, alb, 5.0)


def planks():
    """Vertical weathered planks, 2 m tile: 10 boards across."""
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:N, 0:N].astype(np.float32)
    cols = 10
    cw = N / cols
    col = np.floor(xx / cw).astype(np.int32)
    u = xx / cw - col
    rnd = np.random.default_rng(61).random(cols)[col]
    grain = spectral(N, 1.2, 62, lo=4, aniso=(1.0, 0.08))
    grain2 = spectral(N, 1.0, 63, lo=30, aniso=(1.0, 0.15))
    gap = 1 - smoothstep(0.0, 0.035, np.minimum(u, 1 - u))
    # a few knots
    f1, _, _ = cells(N, 14, 64, stretch=(1.0, 2.2))
    knot = 1 - smoothstep(2.0, 7.0, f1)
    h = 0.6 + 0.25 * (grain - 0.5) + 0.12 * (grain2 - 0.5) - 0.7 * gap - 0.2 * knot
    alb = 0.45 + 0.2 * rnd + 0.25 * (grain - 0.5) + 0.1 * (grain2 - 0.5) - 0.3 * gap - 0.2 * knot
    pack_detail('planks', h, alb, 4.0)


def bark():
    """Furrowed bark, 1 m tile (v along the trunk)."""
    ridge = spectral(N, 1.4, 71, lo=3, aniso=(1.0, 0.18))
    ridge = 1 - np.abs(ridge - 0.5) * 2
    fine = spectral(N, 1.0, 72, lo=20, aniso=(1.0, 0.4))
    plates = smoothstep(0.3, 0.7, ridge)
    h = 0.75 * plates + 0.25 * fine
    alb = 0.32 + 0.45 * plates + 0.12 * (fine - 0.5)
    lichen = smoothstep(0.72, 0.8, spectral(N, 1.6, 73, lo=3))
    alb = alb + 0.25 * lichen * plates
    pack_detail('bark', h, alb, 7.0)


def fabric():
    """Woven cotton/wool with wear, 0.5 m tile."""
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:N, 0:N].astype(np.float32)
    k = 2 * np.pi * 64 / N
    weave = 0.5 + 0.25 * np.sin(xx * k) * np.sign(np.sin(yy * k / 2)) + 0.25 * np.sin(yy * k) * np.sign(np.sin(xx * k / 2))
    blot = spectral(N, 2.0, 81, lo=1)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.0, 82, lo=40)
    h = 0.5 * weave + 0.3 * fine + 0.2 * blot
    alb = 0.5 + 0.1 * (weave - 0.5) + 0.3 * (blot - 0.5) + 0.08 * (fine - 0.5)
    pack_detail('fabric', h, alb, 2.0)


def concrete():
    """Cast concrete with board marks and pits, 2 m tile."""
    low = spectral(N, 2.1, 91, lo=1)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.1, 92, lo=30)
    yy, _ = np.mgrid[0:N, 0:N].astype(np.float32)
    boards = np.abs(((yy / (N / 8)) % 1.0) - 0.5) * 2
    board_line = 1 - smoothstep(0.92, 0.99, boards)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(93)
    pits = np.zeros((N, N), np.float32)
    for _ in range(900):
        x, y = rng.integers(0, N, 2)
        r = rng.integers(1, 3)
        pits[max(0, y - r):y + r, max(0, x - r):x + r] = 1
    pits = blur(pits, 1)
    grain = spectral(N, 1.2, 94, lo=6, aniso=(1.0, 0.1))
    h = 0.6 + 0.2 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.5 * pits + 0.15 * (board_line - 1) + 0.1 * (grain - 0.5)
    alb = 0.5 + 0.28 * (low - 0.5) + 0.08 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.25 * pits + 0.06 * (grain - 0.5)
    stains = smoothstep(0.6, 0.9, spectral(N, 1.6, 95, lo=2, aniso=(1.0, 0.25)))
    alb -= 0.15 * stains
    pack_detail('concrete', h, alb, 3.0)


def metal():
    """Painted/worn metal, 1 m tile: subtle orange peel, scratches, rust spots."""
    peel = spectral(N, 1.0, 101, lo=40)
    low = spectral(N, 2.0, 102, lo=1)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(103)
    scratch = np.zeros((N, N), np.float32)
    for _ in range(160):
        x, y = rng.random(2) * N
        a = rng.random() * np.pi
        L = rng.integers(10, 70)
        for t in range(L):
            xi = int(x + np.cos(a) * t) % N
            yi = int(y + np.sin(a) * t) % N
            scratch[yi, xi] = 1
    rust = smoothstep(0.7, 0.85, spectral(N, 1.8, 104, lo=3))
    h = 0.5 + 0.08 * (peel - 0.5) - 0.2 * scratch - 0.1 * rust
    alb = 0.5 + 0.18 * (low - 0.5) + 0.25 * scratch - 0.18 * rust
    pack_detail('metal', h, alb, 2.0)


def rock():
    """Weathered granite, 3 m tile: crystals, cracks, lichen."""
    big = spectral(N, 2.0, 111, lo=1)
    mid = spectral(N, 1.5, 112, lo=6)
    crystals = spectral(N, 0.6, 113, lo=80)
    f1, f2, _ = cells(N, 0, 114, grid=(4, 4), jitter=1.0)
    crack = 1 - smoothstep(0.0, 1.5, f2 - f1)
    lichen = smoothstep(0.7, 0.78, spectral(N, 1.7, 115, lo=4))
    h = 0.45 * big + 0.35 * mid + 0.1 * crystals - 0.5 * crack + 0.05 * lichen
    alb = 0.5 + 0.2 * (mid - 0.5) + 0.15 * (crystals - 0.5) + 0.12 * (big - 0.5) - 0.35 * crack + 0.15 * lichen
    pack_detail('rock', h, alb, 5.0)


def foliage():
    """Leaf/needle clumps, 1 m tile."""
    f1, f2, ident = cells(N, 0, 121, grid=(16, 16), jitter=1.0)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 122)
    leaf = smoothstep(0.0, 10.0, f2 - f1)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.0, 123, lo=40)
    h = 0.6 * leaf + 0.25 * rnd + 0.15 * fine
    alb = 0.3 + 0.35 * rnd + 0.3 * leaf * (0.5 + fine * 0.5) - 0.15 * (1 - leaf)
    pack_detail('foliage', h, alb, 4.0)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# terrain ground textures (4 m tile)

def mud():
    """Wet churned mud with stones, ruts and standing water in the hollows."""
    big = spectral(N, 2.2, 201, lo=1)
    mid = spectral(N, 1.6, 202, lo=5)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.0, 203, lo=40)
    f1, f2, ident = cells(N, 220, 204)
    stones = smoothstep(4.0, 1.0, f1) * (per_cell(ident, 205) > 0.55)
    h = 0.45 * big + 0.35 * mid + 0.1 * fine + 0.35 * stones
    h = np.clip(h / h.max(), 0, 1)
    dark, light, stone_c = lin('#2e241b'), lin('#5a4836'), lin('#6e675c')
    alb = mix(dark, light, np.clip(0.3 + 0.6 * mid + 0.2 * (fine - 0.5), 0, 1))
    alb = mix(alb, stone_c, stones * 0.9)
    rough = 0.55 + 0.35 * mid - 0.3 * (1 - h)
    pack_ground('mud', alb, h, rough, 6.0)


def grass():
    """Wet meadow grass, dark green-brown with clumps and dead patches."""
    big = spectral(N, 2.0, 211, lo=1)
    mid = spectral(N, 1.4, 212, lo=6)
    blades = spectral(N, 0.8, 213, lo=60, aniso=(1.0, 0.35))
    blades2 = spectral(N, 0.8, 214, lo=60, aniso=(0.35, 1.0))
    bl = np.maximum(blades, blades2)
    dead = smoothstep(0.62, 0.8, big)
    h = 0.35 * mid + 0.55 * bl + 0.1 * big
    g_dark, g_light, g_dead, soil = lin('#1f2a15'), lin('#4c5a2c'), lin('#6a5c38'), lin('#33291e')
    alb = mix(g_dark, g_light, np.clip(bl * 0.9 + 0.2 * (mid - 0.5), 0, 1))
    alb = mix(alb, g_dead, dead * 0.6)
    alb = mix(alb, soil, smoothstep(0.35, 0.15, bl) * 0.5)
    rough = 0.75 + 0.2 * mid
    pack_ground('grass', alb, h, rough, 5.0)


def forest():
    """Forest floor: needles, leaf litter, twigs, moss patches."""
    big = spectral(N, 2.1, 221, lo=1)
    mid = spectral(N, 1.4, 222, lo=6)
    f1, f2, ident = cells(N, 0, 223, grid=(28, 28), jitter=1.0)
    leaves = smoothstep(0.0, 4.0, f2 - f1) * (per_cell(ident, 224) > 0.35)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 225)
    needles = spectral(N, 0.7, 226, lo=90, aniso=(1.0, 0.25))
    needles2 = spectral(N, 0.7, 227, lo=90, aniso=(0.25, 1.0))
    nd = np.maximum(needles, needles2)
    moss = smoothstep(0.62, 0.75, big)
    h = 0.35 * leaves + 0.35 * nd + 0.2 * mid + 0.1 * rnd
    soil, needle_c, leaf_a, leaf_b, moss_c = (lin('#241b13'), lin('#5b4027'), lin('#5e4a2c'),
                                              lin('#3d2f1f'), lin('#3c4a24'))
    alb = mix(soil, needle_c, np.clip(nd * 1.1, 0, 1))
    alb = mix(alb, mix(leaf_a, leaf_b, rnd), leaves * 0.8)
    alb = mix(alb, moss_c, moss * 0.7)
    rough = 0.7 + 0.25 * mid
    pack_ground('forest', alb, h, rough, 5.0)


def cobble():
    """Village street cobbles (setts) with mud in the joints, 4 m tile."""
    f1, f2, ident = cells(N, 0, 231, grid=(22, 22), jitter=0.55)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 232)
    edge = f2 - f1
    dome = smoothstep(0.0, 9.0, edge) ** 0.7
    fine = spectral(N, 1.2, 233, lo=20)
    big = spectral(N, 2.2, 234, lo=1)
    h = 0.85 * dome + 0.1 * fine + 0.05 * rnd
    stone_a, stone_b, joint = lin('#5d5952'), lin('#7a756b'), lin('#2a221a')
    alb = mix(stone_a, stone_b, np.clip(rnd * 0.8 + 0.3 * (fine - 0.5), 0, 1))
    alb = alb * (0.85 + 0.3 * big)[..., None]
    alb = mix(alb, joint, 1 - smoothstep(0.5, 3.5, edge))
    rough = 0.45 + 0.4 * (1 - dome)
    pack_ground('cobble', alb, h, rough, 6.0)


ALL = dict(stone=stone, plaster=plaster, brick=brick, tile=tile, slate=slate, planks=planks,
           bark=bark, fabric=fabric, concrete=concrete, metal=metal, rock=rock, foliage=foliage,
           mud=mud, grass=grass, forest=forest, cobble=cobble)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    names = sys.argv[1:] or list(ALL)
    for n in names:
        ALL[n]()

"""Hedgerow — tileable detail textures.

    python3 fun/hedgerow/tools/textures.py            # all
    python3 fun/hedgerow/tools/textures.py stone mud  # some

Writes `assets/textures/<name>.webp` (512², tileable, lossy WebP).

Two kinds:

* detail textures for models (stone, plaster, brick, tile, slate, planks,
  bark, fabric, concrete, metal, rock, foliage): RGB = tangent-space normal,
  A = albedo detail (0.5 = the palette colour, darker below, lighter above).
  The game tints them with each material's palette colour.
* ground textures for the terrain (mud, grass, forest, cobble): RGB = albedo
  (sRGB), A = height; their normals come from `<name>_n.webp` (RGB normal,
  A = roughness).

Everything is built from periodic pieces (spectral noise from filtered white
noise, cell noise with wrap-around distances, np.roll), so every texture
tiles. Deterministic: fixed seeds.
"""
import os, sys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
OUT = os.path.join(HERE, '..', 'assets', 'textures')
N = 512


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# periodic building blocks

def spectral(n, beta, seed, lo=1.0, hi=None, aniso=(1.0, 1.0)):
    """Tileable fractal noise: white noise filtered by 1/f^beta. aniso
    stretches the spectrum (x, y) for streaky noise. Returns 0..1."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    w = rng.standard_normal((n, n))
    F = np.fft.fft2(w)
    fy = np.fft.fftfreq(n)[:, None] * n * aniso[1]
    fx = np.fft.fftfreq(n)[None, :] * n * aniso[0]
    f = np.sqrt(fx * fx + fy * fy)
    f[0, 0] = 1.0
    amp = 1.0 / np.power(f, beta)
    amp[f < lo] = 0.0
    if hi is not None:
        amp *= np.exp(-(f / hi) ** 2)
    out = np.real(np.fft.ifft2(F * amp))
    out -= out.min()
    out /= max(out.max(), 1e-9)
    return out


def cells(n, count, seed, stretch=(1.0, 1.0), jitter=1.0, grid=None):
    """Periodic Worley noise. Returns (F1, F2, id) with distances in pixels.
    `grid` = (gx, gy) places one point per grid cell (jittered) instead of
    uniformly random points."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    if grid:
        gx, gy = grid
        xs, ys = np.meshgrid(np.arange(gx), np.arange(gy))
        px = (xs.ravel() + 0.5 + (rng.random(gx * gy) - 0.5) * jitter) * n / gx
        py = (ys.ravel() + 0.5 + (rng.random(gx * gy) - 0.5) * jitter) * n / gy
    else:
        px = rng.random(count) * n
        py = rng.random(count) * n
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:n, 0:n].astype(np.float32)
    f1 = np.full((n, n), 1e9, np.float32)
    f2 = np.full((n, n), 1e9, np.float32)
    ident = np.zeros((n, n), np.int32)
    sx, sy = stretch
    for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(px, py)):
        dx = np.abs(xx - x)
        dx = np.minimum(dx, n - dx) / sx
        dy = np.abs(yy - y)
        dy = np.minimum(dy, n - dy) / sy
        d = np.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)
        closer = d < f1
        f2 = np.where(closer, f1, np.minimum(f2, d))
        ident = np.where(closer, i, ident)
        f1 = np.where(closer, d, f1)
    return f1, f2, ident


def smoothstep(a, b, x):
    t = np.clip((x - a) / (b - a), 0.0, 1.0)
    return t * t * (3 - 2 * t)


def blur(img, r):
    """Periodic box-ish blur (three box passes ~ gaussian)."""
    out = img.astype(np.float32)
    for _ in range(3):
        acc = np.zeros_like(out)
        for d in range(-r, r + 1):
            acc += np.roll(out, d, axis=1)
        out = acc / (2 * r + 1)
        acc = np.zeros_like(out)
        for d in range(-r, r + 1):
            acc += np.roll(out, d, axis=0)
        out = acc / (2 * r + 1)
    return out


def normal_from_height(h, strength):
    """Tangent-space normal (OpenGL convention, +Y up in the image = -row)."""
    dx = (np.roll(h, -1, axis=1) - np.roll(h, 1, axis=1)) * 0.5
    dy = (np.roll(h, 1, axis=0) - np.roll(h, -1, axis=0)) * 0.5
    nx = -dx * strength
    ny = -dy * strength
    nz = np.ones_like(h)
    l = np.sqrt(nx * nx + ny * ny + nz * nz)
    return np.stack([nx / l, ny / l, nz / l], axis=-1)


def per_cell(ident, seed, count=None):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    vals = rng.random(int(ident.max()) + 1)
    return vals[ident]


def rect_layout(n, rows, cols, seed, offset_rows=True, jitter=0.0, widths=None):
    """Row/column brick-like layout: returns (u, v) within each cell (0..1),
    cell id, and distance to the cell edge in pixels (min of x and y)."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:n, 0:n].astype(np.float32)
    rh = n / rows
    row = np.floor(yy / rh).astype(np.int32)
    v = (yy - row * rh) / rh
    shift = np.where(row % 2 == 1, 0.5, 0.0) if offset_rows else 0.0
    row_jit = rng.random(rows) * jitter
    cw = n / cols
    xs = (xx / cw + shift + row_jit[row]) % cols
    col = np.floor(xs).astype(np.int32)
    u = xs - col
    ident = row * cols + col
    ex = np.minimum(u, 1 - u) * cw
    ey = np.minimum(v, 1 - v) * rh
    return u, v, ident, np.minimum(ex, ey), ex, ey


def pack_detail(name, height, albedo, strength):
    """RGB = normal from height, A = albedo detail (0..1, 0.5 neutral)."""
    nrm = normal_from_height(height, strength)
    rgb = ((nrm * 0.5 + 0.5) * 255).clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    a = (np.clip(albedo, 0, 1) * 255).astype(np.uint8)
    img = np.dstack([rgb, a])
    save(name, img)


def pack_ground(name, albedo_rgb, height, rough, strength):
    rgb = (np.clip(albedo_rgb, 0, 1) ** (1 / 2.2) * 255).astype(np.uint8)
    a = (np.clip(height, 0, 1) * 255).astype(np.uint8)
    save(name, np.dstack([rgb, a]))
    nrm = normal_from_height(height, strength)
    nrgb = ((nrm * 0.5 + 0.5) * 255).clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    save(name + '_n', np.dstack([nrgb, (np.clip(rough, 0, 1) * 255).astype(np.uint8)]))


def save(name, img):
    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(OUT, name + '.webp')
    Image.fromarray(img, 'RGBA').save(path, 'WEBP', quality=88, method=6, exact=True)
    print(f'{name:10s} {os.path.getsize(path) // 1024:4d} KB')


def lin(hexcode):
    c = np.array([int(hexcode[i:i + 2], 16) / 255 for i in (1, 3, 5)])
    return np.where(c <= 0.04045, c / 12.92, ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4)


def mix(a, b, t):
    t = t[..., None] if np.ndim(t) == 2 else t
    return a * (1 - t) + b * t


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# model detail textures (tile = see materials.js for metres per tile)

def stone():
    """Rubble masonry, ~2 m tile: irregular stones in rough courses, mortar."""
    f1, f2, ident = cells(N, 0, 11, stretch=(1.35, 1.0), jitter=0.9, grid=(9, 12))
    edge = f2 - f1
    mortar = 1 - smoothstep(1.5, 6.0, edge)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 12)
    bulge = smoothstep(0.0, 14.0, edge) ** 0.6
    fine = spectral(N, 1.6, 13, lo=4)
    grain = spectral(N, 1.0, 14, lo=40)
    h = bulge * (0.7 + 0.3 * rnd) + 0.25 * fine + 0.08 * grain
    h = h * (1 - 0.8 * mortar)
    alb = 0.42 + 0.22 * rnd + 0.18 * (fine - 0.5) + 0.08 * (grain - 0.5)
    alb = alb * (1 - 0.35 * mortar) + 0.08 * mortar
    pack_detail('stone', h, alb, 5.0)


def plaster():
    """Lime plaster, ~2 m tile: blotches, trowel marks, hairline cracks,
    a few patches fallen off."""
    low = spectral(N, 2.2, 21, lo=1)
    mid = spectral(N, 1.5, 22, lo=6)
    fine = spectral(N, 0.9, 23, lo=60)
    f1, f2, _ = cells(N, 0, 24, grid=(5, 5), jitter=1.0)
    crack = 1 - smoothstep(0.0, 1.2, f2 - f1)
    crack *= smoothstep(0.55, 0.75, spectral(N, 2.0, 25, lo=2))
    patch = smoothstep(0.78, 0.82, spectral(N, 2.4, 26, lo=2))
    h = 0.5 + 0.25 * (mid - 0.5) + 0.12 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.5 * crack - 0.35 * patch
    alb = 0.5 + 0.28 * (low - 0.5) + 0.1 * (mid - 0.5) + 0.06 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.3 * crack - 0.18 * patch
    pack_detail('plaster', h, alb, 3.0)


def brick():
    """Brick, 1 m tile: 4 bricks across, 14 courses."""
    u, v, ident, edge, ex, ey = rect_layout(N, 14, 4, 31)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 32)
    mortar = 1 - smoothstep(1.0, 3.0, edge)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.3, 33, lo=8)
    chips = smoothstep(0.72, 0.8, spectral(N, 1.8, 34, lo=4))
    h = (smoothstep(0, 5, edge) * 0.8 + 0.2 * fine) * (1 - mortar) - 0.25 * chips
    alb = 0.38 + 0.3 * rnd + 0.12 * (fine - 0.5)
    alb = alb * (1 - mortar) + 0.62 * mortar
    pack_detail('brick', h, alb, 4.0)


def tile():
    """Barrel (Roman) roof tiles, 2 m tile: 8 channels across, 10 courses."""
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:N, 0:N].astype(np.float32)
    rows, cols = 10, 8
    rh, cw = N / rows, N / cols
    row = np.floor(yy / rh)
    v = (yy - row * rh) / rh
    shift = np.where(row % 2 == 1, 0.5, 0.0)
    xs = xx / cw + shift
    col = np.floor(xs)
    u = xs - col
    ident = (row * cols + (col % cols)).astype(np.int32)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 41)
    curve = np.sin(u * np.pi) ** 0.7
    # each course overlaps the one below: the lower edge is raised, a shadow above it
    overlap = smoothstep(0.0, 0.25, v) * (1 - 0.6 * smoothstep(0.85, 1.0, v))
    fine = spectral(N, 1.4, 42, lo=8)
    h = 0.55 * curve + 0.35 * (1 - v) + 0.1 * fine
    alb = 0.45 + 0.25 * rnd + 0.12 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.25 * (1 - overlap) - 0.15 * (1 - curve)
    lichen = smoothstep(0.7, 0.8, spectral(N, 1.8, 43, lo=3))
    alb = alb * (1 - 0.3 * lichen)
    pack_detail('tile', h, alb, 6.0)


def slate():
    """Slate roof, 2 m tile: 9 courses of staggered rectangular slates."""
    u, v, ident, edge, ex, ey = rect_layout(N, 9, 7, 51, jitter=0.15)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 52)
    gap = 1 - smoothstep(0.5, 2.0, ex)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.2, 53, lo=10, aniso=(1.0, 0.4))
    h = (1 - v) * 0.6 + 0.15 * fine - 0.4 * gap
    alb = 0.45 + 0.18 * rnd + 0.1 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.3 * smoothstep(0.85, 1.0, v) - 0.25 * gap
    pack_detail('slate', h, alb, 5.0)


def planks():
    """Vertical weathered planks, 2 m tile: 10 boards across."""
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:N, 0:N].astype(np.float32)
    cols = 10
    cw = N / cols
    col = np.floor(xx / cw).astype(np.int32)
    u = xx / cw - col
    rnd = np.random.default_rng(61).random(cols)[col]
    grain = spectral(N, 1.2, 62, lo=4, aniso=(1.0, 0.08))
    grain2 = spectral(N, 1.0, 63, lo=30, aniso=(1.0, 0.15))
    gap = 1 - smoothstep(0.0, 0.035, np.minimum(u, 1 - u))
    # a few knots
    f1, _, _ = cells(N, 14, 64, stretch=(1.0, 2.2))
    knot = 1 - smoothstep(2.0, 7.0, f1)
    h = 0.6 + 0.25 * (grain - 0.5) + 0.12 * (grain2 - 0.5) - 0.7 * gap - 0.2 * knot
    alb = 0.45 + 0.2 * rnd + 0.25 * (grain - 0.5) + 0.1 * (grain2 - 0.5) - 0.3 * gap - 0.2 * knot
    pack_detail('planks', h, alb, 4.0)


def bark():
    """Furrowed bark, 1 m tile (v along the trunk)."""
    ridge = spectral(N, 1.4, 71, lo=3, aniso=(1.0, 0.18))
    ridge = 1 - np.abs(ridge - 0.5) * 2
    fine = spectral(N, 1.0, 72, lo=20, aniso=(1.0, 0.4))
    plates = smoothstep(0.3, 0.7, ridge)
    h = 0.75 * plates + 0.25 * fine
    alb = 0.32 + 0.45 * plates + 0.12 * (fine - 0.5)
    lichen = smoothstep(0.72, 0.8, spectral(N, 1.6, 73, lo=3))
    alb = alb + 0.25 * lichen * plates
    pack_detail('bark', h, alb, 7.0)


def fabric():
    """Woven cotton/wool with wear, 0.5 m tile."""
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:N, 0:N].astype(np.float32)
    k = 2 * np.pi * 64 / N
    weave = 0.5 + 0.25 * np.sin(xx * k) * np.sign(np.sin(yy * k / 2)) + 0.25 * np.sin(yy * k) * np.sign(np.sin(xx * k / 2))
    blot = spectral(N, 2.0, 81, lo=1)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.0, 82, lo=40)
    h = 0.5 * weave + 0.3 * fine + 0.2 * blot
    alb = 0.5 + 0.1 * (weave - 0.5) + 0.3 * (blot - 0.5) + 0.08 * (fine - 0.5)
    pack_detail('fabric', h, alb, 2.0)


def concrete():
    """Cast concrete with board marks and pits, 2 m tile."""
    low = spectral(N, 2.1, 91, lo=1)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.1, 92, lo=30)
    yy, _ = np.mgrid[0:N, 0:N].astype(np.float32)
    boards = np.abs(((yy / (N / 8)) % 1.0) - 0.5) * 2
    board_line = 1 - smoothstep(0.92, 0.99, boards)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(93)
    pits = np.zeros((N, N), np.float32)
    for _ in range(900):
        x, y = rng.integers(0, N, 2)
        r = rng.integers(1, 3)
        pits[max(0, y - r):y + r, max(0, x - r):x + r] = 1
    pits = blur(pits, 1)
    grain = spectral(N, 1.2, 94, lo=6, aniso=(1.0, 0.1))
    h = 0.6 + 0.2 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.5 * pits + 0.15 * (board_line - 1) + 0.1 * (grain - 0.5)
    alb = 0.5 + 0.28 * (low - 0.5) + 0.08 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.25 * pits + 0.06 * (grain - 0.5)
    stains = smoothstep(0.6, 0.9, spectral(N, 1.6, 95, lo=2, aniso=(1.0, 0.25)))
    alb -= 0.15 * stains
    pack_detail('concrete', h, alb, 3.0)


def metal():
    """Painted/worn metal, 1 m tile: subtle orange peel, scratches, rust spots."""
    peel = spectral(N, 1.0, 101, lo=40)
    low = spectral(N, 2.0, 102, lo=1)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(103)
    scratch = np.zeros((N, N), np.float32)
    for _ in range(160):
        x, y = rng.random(2) * N
        a = rng.random() * np.pi
        L = rng.integers(10, 70)
        for t in range(L):
            xi = int(x + np.cos(a) * t) % N
            yi = int(y + np.sin(a) * t) % N
            scratch[yi, xi] = 1
    rust = smoothstep(0.7, 0.85, spectral(N, 1.8, 104, lo=3))
    h = 0.5 + 0.08 * (peel - 0.5) - 0.2 * scratch - 0.1 * rust
    alb = 0.5 + 0.18 * (low - 0.5) + 0.25 * scratch - 0.18 * rust
    pack_detail('metal', h, alb, 2.0)


def rock():
    """Weathered granite, 3 m tile: crystals, cracks, lichen."""
    big = spectral(N, 2.0, 111, lo=1)
    mid = spectral(N, 1.5, 112, lo=6)
    crystals = spectral(N, 0.6, 113, lo=80)
    f1, f2, _ = cells(N, 0, 114, grid=(4, 4), jitter=1.0)
    crack = 1 - smoothstep(0.0, 1.5, f2 - f1)
    lichen = smoothstep(0.7, 0.78, spectral(N, 1.7, 115, lo=4))
    h = 0.45 * big + 0.35 * mid + 0.1 * crystals - 0.5 * crack + 0.05 * lichen
    alb = 0.5 + 0.2 * (mid - 0.5) + 0.15 * (crystals - 0.5) + 0.12 * (big - 0.5) - 0.35 * crack + 0.15 * lichen
    pack_detail('rock', h, alb, 5.0)


def foliage():
    """Leaf/needle clumps, 1 m tile."""
    f1, f2, ident = cells(N, 0, 121, grid=(16, 16), jitter=1.0)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 122)
    leaf = smoothstep(0.0, 10.0, f2 - f1)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.0, 123, lo=40)
    h = 0.6 * leaf + 0.25 * rnd + 0.15 * fine
    alb = 0.3 + 0.35 * rnd + 0.3 * leaf * (0.5 + fine * 0.5) - 0.15 * (1 - leaf)
    pack_detail('foliage', h, alb, 4.0)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# terrain ground textures (4 m tile)

def mud():
    """Wet churned mud with stones, ruts and standing water in the hollows."""
    big = spectral(N, 2.2, 201, lo=1)
    mid = spectral(N, 1.6, 202, lo=5)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.0, 203, lo=40)
    f1, f2, ident = cells(N, 220, 204)
    stones = smoothstep(4.0, 1.0, f1) * (per_cell(ident, 205) > 0.55)
    h = 0.45 * big + 0.35 * mid + 0.1 * fine + 0.35 * stones
    h = np.clip(h / h.max(), 0, 1)
    dark, light, stone_c = lin('#2e241b'), lin('#5a4836'), lin('#6e675c')
    alb = mix(dark, light, np.clip(0.3 + 0.6 * mid + 0.2 * (fine - 0.5), 0, 1))
    alb = mix(alb, stone_c, stones * 0.9)
    rough = 0.55 + 0.35 * mid - 0.3 * (1 - h)
    pack_ground('mud', alb, h, rough, 6.0)


def grass():
    """Wet meadow grass, dark green-brown with clumps and dead patches."""
    big = spectral(N, 2.0, 211, lo=1)
    mid = spectral(N, 1.4, 212, lo=6)
    blades = spectral(N, 0.8, 213, lo=60, aniso=(1.0, 0.35))
    blades2 = spectral(N, 0.8, 214, lo=60, aniso=(0.35, 1.0))
    bl = np.maximum(blades, blades2)
    dead = smoothstep(0.62, 0.8, big)
    h = 0.35 * mid + 0.55 * bl + 0.1 * big
    g_dark, g_light, g_dead, soil = lin('#1f2a15'), lin('#4c5a2c'), lin('#6a5c38'), lin('#33291e')
    alb = mix(g_dark, g_light, np.clip(bl * 0.9 + 0.2 * (mid - 0.5), 0, 1))
    alb = mix(alb, g_dead, dead * 0.6)
    alb = mix(alb, soil, smoothstep(0.35, 0.15, bl) * 0.5)
    rough = 0.75 + 0.2 * mid
    pack_ground('grass', alb, h, rough, 5.0)


def forest():
    """Forest floor: needles, leaf litter, twigs, moss patches."""
    big = spectral(N, 2.1, 221, lo=1)
    mid = spectral(N, 1.4, 222, lo=6)
    f1, f2, ident = cells(N, 0, 223, grid=(28, 28), jitter=1.0)
    leaves = smoothstep(0.0, 4.0, f2 - f1) * (per_cell(ident, 224) > 0.35)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 225)
    needles = spectral(N, 0.7, 226, lo=90, aniso=(1.0, 0.25))
    needles2 = spectral(N, 0.7, 227, lo=90, aniso=(0.25, 1.0))
    nd = np.maximum(needles, needles2)
    moss = smoothstep(0.62, 0.75, big)
    h = 0.35 * leaves + 0.35 * nd + 0.2 * mid + 0.1 * rnd
    soil, needle_c, leaf_a, leaf_b, moss_c = (lin('#241b13'), lin('#5b4027'), lin('#5e4a2c'),
                                              lin('#3d2f1f'), lin('#3c4a24'))
    alb = mix(soil, needle_c, np.clip(nd * 1.1, 0, 1))
    alb = mix(alb, mix(leaf_a, leaf_b, rnd), leaves * 0.8)
    alb = mix(alb, moss_c, moss * 0.7)
    rough = 0.7 + 0.25 * mid
    pack_ground('forest', alb, h, rough, 5.0)


def cobble():
    """Village street cobbles (setts) with mud in the joints, 4 m tile."""
    f1, f2, ident = cells(N, 0, 231, grid=(22, 22), jitter=0.55)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 232)
    edge = f2 - f1
    dome = smoothstep(0.0, 9.0, edge) ** 0.7
    fine = spectral(N, 1.2, 233, lo=20)
    big = spectral(N, 2.2, 234, lo=1)
    h = 0.85 * dome + 0.1 * fine + 0.05 * rnd
    stone_a, stone_b, joint = lin('#5d5952'), lin('#7a756b'), lin('#2a221a')
    alb = mix(stone_a, stone_b, np.clip(rnd * 0.8 + 0.3 * (fine - 0.5), 0, 1))
    alb = alb * (0.85 + 0.3 * big)[..., None]
    alb = mix(alb, joint, 1 - smoothstep(0.5, 3.5, edge))
    rough = 0.45 + 0.4 * (1 - dome)
    pack_ground('cobble', alb, h, rough, 6.0)

"""Hedgerow — tileable detail textures.

    python3 fun/hedgerow/tools/textures.py            # all
    python3 fun/hedgerow/tools/textures.py stone mud  # some

Writes `assets/textures/<name>.webp` (512², tileable, lossy WebP).

Two kinds:

* detail textures for models (stone, plaster, brick, tile, slate, planks,
  bark, fabric, concrete, metal, rock, foliage): RGB = tangent-space normal,
  A = albedo detail (0.5 = the palette colour, darker below, lighter above).
  The game tints them with each material's palette colour.
* ground textures for the terrain (mud, grass, forest, cobble): RGB = albedo
  (sRGB), A = height; their normals come from `<name>_n.webp` (RGB normal,
  A = roughness).

Everything is built from periodic pieces (spectral noise from filtered white
noise, cell noise with wrap-around distances, np.roll), so every texture
tiles. Deterministic: fixed seeds.
"""
import os, sys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
OUT = os.path.join(HERE, '..', 'assets', 'textures')
N = 512


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# periodic building blocks

def spectral(n, beta, seed, lo=1.0, hi=None, aniso=(1.0, 1.0)):
    """Tileable fractal noise: white noise filtered by 1/f^beta. aniso
    stretches the spectrum (x, y) for streaky noise. Returns 0..1."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    w = rng.standard_normal((n, n))
    F = np.fft.fft2(w)
    fy = np.fft.fftfreq(n)[:, None] * n * aniso[1]
    fx = np.fft.fftfreq(n)[None, :] * n * aniso[0]
    f = np.sqrt(fx * fx + fy * fy)
    f[0, 0] = 1.0
    amp = 1.0 / np.power(f, beta)
    amp[f < lo] = 0.0
    if hi is not None:
        amp *= np.exp(-(f / hi) ** 2)
    out = np.real(np.fft.ifft2(F * amp))
    out -= out.min()
    out /= max(out.max(), 1e-9)
    return out


def cells(n, count, seed, stretch=(1.0, 1.0), jitter=1.0, grid=None):
    """Periodic Worley noise. Returns (F1, F2, id) with distances in pixels.
    `grid` = (gx, gy) places one point per grid cell (jittered) instead of
    uniformly random points."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    if grid:
        gx, gy = grid
        xs, ys = np.meshgrid(np.arange(gx), np.arange(gy))
        px = (xs.ravel() + 0.5 + (rng.random(gx * gy) - 0.5) * jitter) * n / gx
        py = (ys.ravel() + 0.5 + (rng.random(gx * gy) - 0.5) * jitter) * n / gy
    else:
        px = rng.random(count) * n
        py = rng.random(count) * n
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:n, 0:n].astype(np.float32)
    f1 = np.full((n, n), 1e9, np.float32)
    f2 = np.full((n, n), 1e9, np.float32)
    ident = np.zeros((n, n), np.int32)
    sx, sy = stretch
    for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(px, py)):
        dx = np.abs(xx - x)
        dx = np.minimum(dx, n - dx) / sx
        dy = np.abs(yy - y)
        dy = np.minimum(dy, n - dy) / sy
        d = np.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)
        closer = d < f1
        f2 = np.where(closer, f1, np.minimum(f2, d))
        ident = np.where(closer, i, ident)
        f1 = np.where(closer, d, f1)
    return f1, f2, ident


def smoothstep(a, b, x):
    t = np.clip((x - a) / (b - a), 0.0, 1.0)
    return t * t * (3 - 2 * t)


def blur(img, r):
    """Periodic box-ish blur (three box passes ~ gaussian)."""
    out = img.astype(np.float32)
    for _ in range(3):
        acc = np.zeros_like(out)
        for d in range(-r, r + 1):
            acc += np.roll(out, d, axis=1)
        out = acc / (2 * r + 1)
        acc = np.zeros_like(out)
        for d in range(-r, r + 1):
            acc += np.roll(out, d, axis=0)
        out = acc / (2 * r + 1)
    return out


def normal_from_height(h, strength):
    """Tangent-space normal (OpenGL convention, +Y up in the image = -row)."""
    dx = (np.roll(h, -1, axis=1) - np.roll(h, 1, axis=1)) * 0.5
    dy = (np.roll(h, 1, axis=0) - np.roll(h, -1, axis=0)) * 0.5
    nx = -dx * strength
    ny = -dy * strength
    nz = np.ones_like(h)
    l = np.sqrt(nx * nx + ny * ny + nz * nz)
    return np.stack([nx / l, ny / l, nz / l], axis=-1)


def per_cell(ident, seed, count=None):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    vals = rng.random(int(ident.max()) + 1)
    return vals[ident]


def rect_layout(n, rows, cols, seed, offset_rows=True, jitter=0.0, widths=None):
    """Row/column brick-like layout: returns (u, v) within each cell (0..1),
    cell id, and distance to the cell edge in pixels (min of x and y)."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:n, 0:n].astype(np.float32)
    rh = n / rows
    row = np.floor(yy / rh).astype(np.int32)
    v = (yy - row * rh) / rh
    shift = np.where(row % 2 == 1, 0.5, 0.0) if offset_rows else 0.0
    row_jit = rng.random(rows) * jitter
    cw = n / cols
    xs = (xx / cw + shift + row_jit[row]) % cols
    col = np.floor(xs).astype(np.int32)
    u = xs - col
    ident = row * cols + col
    ex = np.minimum(u, 1 - u) * cw
    ey = np.minimum(v, 1 - v) * rh
    return u, v, ident, np.minimum(ex, ey), ex, ey


def pack_detail(name, height, albedo, strength):
    """RGB = normal from height, A = albedo detail (0..1, 0.5 neutral)."""
    nrm = normal_from_height(height, strength)
    rgb = ((nrm * 0.5 + 0.5) * 255).clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    a = (np.clip(albedo, 0, 1) * 255).astype(np.uint8)
    img = np.dstack([rgb, a])
    save(name, img)


def pack_ground(name, albedo_rgb, height, rough, strength):
    rgb = (np.clip(albedo_rgb, 0, 1) ** (1 / 2.2) * 255).astype(np.uint8)
    a = (np.clip(height, 0, 1) * 255).astype(np.uint8)
    save(name, np.dstack([rgb, a]))
    nrm = normal_from_height(height, strength)
    nrgb = ((nrm * 0.5 + 0.5) * 255).clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    save(name + '_n', np.dstack([nrgb, (np.clip(rough, 0, 1) * 255).astype(np.uint8)]))


def save(name, img):
    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(OUT, name + '.webp')
    Image.fromarray(img, 'RGBA').save(path, 'WEBP', quality=88, method=6, exact=True)
    print(f'{name:10s} {os.path.getsize(path) // 1024:4d} KB')


def lin(hexcode):
    c = np.array([int(hexcode[i:i + 2], 16) / 255 for i in (1, 3, 5)])
    return np.where(c <= 0.04045, c / 12.92, ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4)


def mix(a, b, t):
    t = t[..., None] if np.ndim(t) == 2 else t
    return a * (1 - t) + b * t


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# model detail textures (tile = see materials.js for metres per tile)

def stone():
    """Rubble masonry, ~2 m tile: irregular stones in rough courses, mortar."""
    f1, f2, ident = cells(N, 0, 11, stretch=(1.35, 1.0), jitter=0.9, grid=(9, 12))
    edge = f2 - f1
    mortar = 1 - smoothstep(1.5, 6.0, edge)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 12)
    bulge = smoothstep(0.0, 14.0, edge) ** 0.6
    fine = spectral(N, 1.6, 13, lo=4)
    grain = spectral(N, 1.0, 14, lo=40)
    h = bulge * (0.7 + 0.3 * rnd) + 0.25 * fine + 0.08 * grain
    h = h * (1 - 0.8 * mortar)
    alb = 0.42 + 0.22 * rnd + 0.18 * (fine - 0.5) + 0.08 * (grain - 0.5)
    alb = alb * (1 - 0.35 * mortar) + 0.08 * mortar
    pack_detail('stone', h, alb, 5.0)


def plaster():
    """Lime plaster, ~2 m tile: blotches, trowel marks, hairline cracks,
    a few patches fallen off."""
    low = spectral(N, 2.2, 21, lo=1)
    mid = spectral(N, 1.5, 22, lo=6)
    fine = spectral(N, 0.9, 23, lo=60)
    f1, f2, _ = cells(N, 0, 24, grid=(5, 5), jitter=1.0)
    crack = 1 - smoothstep(0.0, 1.2, f2 - f1)
    crack *= smoothstep(0.55, 0.75, spectral(N, 2.0, 25, lo=2))
    patch = smoothstep(0.78, 0.82, spectral(N, 2.4, 26, lo=2))
    h = 0.5 + 0.25 * (mid - 0.5) + 0.12 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.5 * crack - 0.35 * patch
    alb = 0.5 + 0.28 * (low - 0.5) + 0.1 * (mid - 0.5) + 0.06 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.3 * crack - 0.18 * patch
    pack_detail('plaster', h, alb, 3.0)


def brick():
    """Brick, 1 m tile: 4 bricks across, 14 courses."""
    u, v, ident, edge, ex, ey = rect_layout(N, 14, 4, 31)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 32)
    mortar = 1 - smoothstep(1.0, 3.0, edge)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.3, 33, lo=8)
    chips = smoothstep(0.72, 0.8, spectral(N, 1.8, 34, lo=4))
    h = (smoothstep(0, 5, edge) * 0.8 + 0.2 * fine) * (1 - mortar) - 0.25 * chips
    alb = 0.38 + 0.3 * rnd + 0.12 * (fine - 0.5)
    alb = alb * (1 - mortar) + 0.62 * mortar
    pack_detail('brick', h, alb, 4.0)


def tile():
    """Barrel (Roman) roof tiles, 2 m tile: 8 channels across, 10 courses."""
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:N, 0:N].astype(np.float32)
    rows, cols = 10, 8
    rh, cw = N / rows, N / cols
    row = np.floor(yy / rh)
    v = (yy - row * rh) / rh
    shift = np.where(row % 2 == 1, 0.5, 0.0)
    xs = xx / cw + shift
    col = np.floor(xs)
    u = xs - col
    ident = (row * cols + (col % cols)).astype(np.int32)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 41)
    curve = np.sin(u * np.pi) ** 0.7
    # each course overlaps the one below: the lower edge is raised, a shadow above it
    overlap = smoothstep(0.0, 0.25, v) * (1 - 0.6 * smoothstep(0.85, 1.0, v))
    fine = spectral(N, 1.4, 42, lo=8)
    h = 0.55 * curve + 0.35 * (1 - v) + 0.1 * fine
    alb = 0.45 + 0.25 * rnd + 0.12 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.25 * (1 - overlap) - 0.15 * (1 - curve)
    lichen = smoothstep(0.7, 0.8, spectral(N, 1.8, 43, lo=3))
    alb = alb * (1 - 0.3 * lichen)
    pack_detail('tile', h, alb, 6.0)


def slate():
    """Slate roof, 2 m tile: 9 courses of staggered rectangular slates."""
    u, v, ident, edge, ex, ey = rect_layout(N, 9, 7, 51, jitter=0.15)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 52)
    gap = 1 - smoothstep(0.5, 2.0, ex)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.2, 53, lo=10, aniso=(1.0, 0.4))
    h = (1 - v) * 0.6 + 0.15 * fine - 0.4 * gap
    alb = 0.45 + 0.18 * rnd + 0.1 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.3 * smoothstep(0.85, 1.0, v) - 0.25 * gap
    pack_detail('slate', h, alb, 5.0)


def planks():
    """Vertical weathered planks, 2 m tile: 10 boards across."""
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:N, 0:N].astype(np.float32)
    cols = 10
    cw = N / cols
    col = np.floor(xx / cw).astype(np.int32)
    u = xx / cw - col
    rnd = np.random.default_rng(61).random(cols)[col]
    grain = spectral(N, 1.2, 62, lo=4, aniso=(1.0, 0.08))
    grain2 = spectral(N, 1.0, 63, lo=30, aniso=(1.0, 0.15))
    gap = 1 - smoothstep(0.0, 0.035, np.minimum(u, 1 - u))
    # a few knots
    f1, _, _ = cells(N, 14, 64, stretch=(1.0, 2.2))
    knot = 1 - smoothstep(2.0, 7.0, f1)
    h = 0.6 + 0.25 * (grain - 0.5) + 0.12 * (grain2 - 0.5) - 0.7 * gap - 0.2 * knot
    alb = 0.45 + 0.2 * rnd + 0.25 * (grain - 0.5) + 0.1 * (grain2 - 0.5) - 0.3 * gap - 0.2 * knot
    pack_detail('planks', h, alb, 4.0)


def bark():
    """Furrowed bark, 1 m tile (v along the trunk)."""
    ridge = spectral(N, 1.4, 71, lo=3, aniso=(1.0, 0.18))
    ridge = 1 - np.abs(ridge - 0.5) * 2
    fine = spectral(N, 1.0, 72, lo=20, aniso=(1.0, 0.4))
    plates = smoothstep(0.3, 0.7, ridge)
    h = 0.75 * plates + 0.25 * fine
    alb = 0.32 + 0.45 * plates + 0.12 * (fine - 0.5)
    lichen = smoothstep(0.72, 0.8, spectral(N, 1.6, 73, lo=3))
    alb = alb + 0.25 * lichen * plates
    pack_detail('bark', h, alb, 7.0)


def fabric():
    """Woven cotton/wool with wear, 0.5 m tile."""
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:N, 0:N].astype(np.float32)
    k = 2 * np.pi * 64 / N
    weave = 0.5 + 0.25 * np.sin(xx * k) * np.sign(np.sin(yy * k / 2)) + 0.25 * np.sin(yy * k) * np.sign(np.sin(xx * k / 2))
    blot = spectral(N, 2.0, 81, lo=1)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.0, 82, lo=40)
    h = 0.5 * weave + 0.3 * fine + 0.2 * blot
    alb = 0.5 + 0.1 * (weave - 0.5) + 0.3 * (blot - 0.5) + 0.08 * (fine - 0.5)
    pack_detail('fabric', h, alb, 2.0)


def concrete():
    """Cast concrete with board marks and pits, 2 m tile."""
    low = spectral(N, 2.1, 91, lo=1)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.1, 92, lo=30)
    yy, _ = np.mgrid[0:N, 0:N].astype(np.float32)
    boards = np.abs(((yy / (N / 8)) % 1.0) - 0.5) * 2
    board_line = 1 - smoothstep(0.92, 0.99, boards)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(93)
    pits = np.zeros((N, N), np.float32)
    for _ in range(900):
        x, y = rng.integers(0, N, 2)
        r = rng.integers(1, 3)
        pits[max(0, y - r):y + r, max(0, x - r):x + r] = 1
    pits = blur(pits, 1)
    grain = spectral(N, 1.2, 94, lo=6, aniso=(1.0, 0.1))
    h = 0.6 + 0.2 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.5 * pits + 0.15 * (board_line - 1) + 0.1 * (grain - 0.5)
    alb = 0.5 + 0.28 * (low - 0.5) + 0.08 * (fine - 0.5) - 0.25 * pits + 0.06 * (grain - 0.5)
    stains = smoothstep(0.6, 0.9, spectral(N, 1.6, 95, lo=2, aniso=(1.0, 0.25)))
    alb -= 0.15 * stains
    pack_detail('concrete', h, alb, 3.0)


def metal():
    """Painted/worn metal, 1 m tile: subtle orange peel, scratches, rust spots."""
    peel = spectral(N, 1.0, 101, lo=40)
    low = spectral(N, 2.0, 102, lo=1)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(103)
    scratch = np.zeros((N, N), np.float32)
    for _ in range(160):
        x, y = rng.random(2) * N
        a = rng.random() * np.pi
        L = rng.integers(10, 70)
        for t in range(L):
            xi = int(x + np.cos(a) * t) % N
            yi = int(y + np.sin(a) * t) % N
            scratch[yi, xi] = 1
    rust = smoothstep(0.7, 0.85, spectral(N, 1.8, 104, lo=3))
    h = 0.5 + 0.08 * (peel - 0.5) - 0.2 * scratch - 0.1 * rust
    alb = 0.5 + 0.18 * (low - 0.5) + 0.25 * scratch - 0.18 * rust
    pack_detail('metal', h, alb, 2.0)


def rock():
    """Weathered granite, 3 m tile: crystals, cracks, lichen."""
    big = spectral(N, 2.0, 111, lo=1)
    mid = spectral(N, 1.5, 112, lo=6)
    crystals = spectral(N, 0.6, 113, lo=80)
    f1, f2, _ = cells(N, 0, 114, grid=(4, 4), jitter=1.0)
    crack = 1 - smoothstep(0.0, 1.5, f2 - f1)
    lichen = smoothstep(0.7, 0.78, spectral(N, 1.7, 115, lo=4))
    h = 0.45 * big + 0.35 * mid + 0.1 * crystals - 0.5 * crack + 0.05 * lichen
    alb = 0.5 + 0.2 * (mid - 0.5) + 0.15 * (crystals - 0.5) + 0.12 * (big - 0.5) - 0.35 * crack + 0.15 * lichen
    pack_detail('rock', h, alb, 5.0)


def foliage():
    """Leaf/needle clumps, 1 m tile."""
    f1, f2, ident = cells(N, 0, 121, grid=(16, 16), jitter=1.0)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 122)
    leaf = smoothstep(0.0, 10.0, f2 - f1)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.0, 123, lo=40)
    h = 0.6 * leaf + 0.25 * rnd + 0.15 * fine
    alb = 0.3 + 0.35 * rnd + 0.3 * leaf * (0.5 + fine * 0.5) - 0.15 * (1 - leaf)
    pack_detail('foliage', h, alb, 4.0)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# terrain ground textures (4 m tile)

def mud():
    """Wet churned mud with stones, ruts and standing water in the hollows."""
    big = spectral(N, 2.2, 201, lo=1)
    mid = spectral(N, 1.6, 202, lo=5)
    fine = spectral(N, 1.0, 203, lo=40)
    f1, f2, ident = cells(N, 220, 204)
    stones = smoothstep(4.0, 1.0, f1) * (per_cell(ident, 205) > 0.55)
    h = 0.45 * big + 0.35 * mid + 0.1 * fine + 0.35 * stones
    h = np.clip(h / h.max(), 0, 1)
    dark, light, stone_c = lin('#2e241b'), lin('#5a4836'), lin('#6e675c')
    alb = mix(dark, light, np.clip(0.3 + 0.6 * mid + 0.2 * (fine - 0.5), 0, 1))
    alb = mix(alb, stone_c, stones * 0.9)
    rough = 0.55 + 0.35 * mid - 0.3 * (1 - h)
    pack_ground('mud', alb, h, rough, 6.0)


def grass():
    """Wet meadow grass, dark green-brown with clumps and dead patches."""
    big = spectral(N, 2.0, 211, lo=1)
    mid = spectral(N, 1.4, 212, lo=6)
    blades = spectral(N, 0.8, 213, lo=60, aniso=(1.0, 0.35))
    blades2 = spectral(N, 0.8, 214, lo=60, aniso=(0.35, 1.0))
    bl = np.maximum(blades, blades2)
    dead = smoothstep(0.62, 0.8, big)
    h = 0.35 * mid + 0.55 * bl + 0.1 * big
    g_dark, g_light, g_dead, soil = lin('#1f2a15'), lin('#4c5a2c'), lin('#6a5c38'), lin('#33291e')
    alb = mix(g_dark, g_light, np.clip(bl * 0.9 + 0.2 * (mid - 0.5), 0, 1))
    alb = mix(alb, g_dead, dead * 0.6)
    alb = mix(alb, soil, smoothstep(0.35, 0.15, bl) * 0.5)
    rough = 0.75 + 0.2 * mid
    pack_ground('grass', alb, h, rough, 5.0)


def forest():
    """Forest floor: needles, leaf litter, twigs, moss patches."""
    big = spectral(N, 2.1, 221, lo=1)
    mid = spectral(N, 1.4, 222, lo=6)
    f1, f2, ident = cells(N, 0, 223, grid=(28, 28), jitter=1.0)
    leaves = smoothstep(0.0, 4.0, f2 - f1) * (per_cell(ident, 224) > 0.35)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 225)
    needles = spectral(N, 0.7, 226, lo=90, aniso=(1.0, 0.25))
    needles2 = spectral(N, 0.7, 227, lo=90, aniso=(0.25, 1.0))
    nd = np.maximum(needles, needles2)
    moss = smoothstep(0.62, 0.75, big)
    h = 0.35 * leaves + 0.35 * nd + 0.2 * mid + 0.1 * rnd
    soil, needle_c, leaf_a, leaf_b, moss_c = (lin('#241b13'), lin('#5b4027'), lin('#5e4a2c'),
                                              lin('#3d2f1f'), lin('#3c4a24'))
    alb = mix(soil, needle_c, np.clip(nd * 1.1, 0, 1))
    alb = mix(alb, mix(leaf_a, leaf_b, rnd), leaves * 0.8)
    alb = mix(alb, moss_c, moss * 0.7)
    rough = 0.7 + 0.25 * mid
    pack_ground('forest', alb, h, rough, 5.0)


def cobble():
    """Village street cobbles (setts) with mud in the joints, 4 m tile."""
    f1, f2, ident = cells(N, 0, 231, grid=(22, 22), jitter=0.55)
    rnd = per_cell(ident, 232)
    edge = f2 - f1
    dome = smoothstep(0.0, 9.0, edge) ** 0.7
    fine = spectral(N, 1.2, 233, lo=20)
    big = spectral(N, 2.2, 234, lo=1)
    h = 0.85 * dome + 0.1 * fine + 0.05 * rnd
    stone_a, stone_b, joint = lin('#5d5952'), lin('#7a756b'), lin('#2a221a')
    alb = mix(stone_a, stone_b, np.clip(rnd * 0.8 + 0.3 * (fine - 0.5), 0, 1))
    alb = alb * (0.85 + 0.3 * big)[..., None]
    alb = mix(alb, joint, 1 - smoothstep(0.5, 3.5, edge))
    rough = 0.45 + 0.4 * (1 - dome)
    pack_ground('cobble', alb, h, rough, 6.0)


ALL = dict(stone=stone, plaster=plaster, brick=brick, tile=tile, slate=slate, planks=planks,
           bark=bark, fabric=fabric, concrete=concrete, metal=metal, rock=rock, foliage=foliage,
           mud=mud, grass=grass, forest=forest, cobble=cobble)

    names = sys.argv[1:] or list(ALL)

        ALL[n]()

## What the game must know

* **Origins.** Trees, bushes, stumps and ground cover: origin at the trunk /
  clump centre on the ground (z = 0), so the crown may be a little off
  centre (lean). Hedges: centred, base on the ground. Boulders and the
  outcrop are **partly sunk**: their lowest vertex is below z = 0 (boulders
  ~12 % of their height, outcrop ~0.45 m) so they sit into uneven terrain;
  sizes above include the sunk part.
* **LODs.** `*_lod` nodes share the full node's silhouette and colours and
  have **no colliders** — register colliders from the full node only. Swap
  at ~60–90 m (fog hides the rest).
* **Instancing.** Every tree/grass node is a single mesh with ≤ 2 primitives
  (bark + foliage) — suitable for `InstancedMesh` per primitive. Random yaw
  per instance is fine for everything except `log_bridge` and hedges.
* **Hedges** tile along X every **4.0 m**: the leaf body overhangs each end
  by ~0.3–0.45 m with tapered ends, so neighbours overlap and hide the joint
  (a 180° yaw on alternate segments hides repetition). Collider: one solid
  box (blocks movement, bullets and sight — bocage is impassable);
  `hedge_low` (top 1.15 m) is vaultable.
* **Bushes** use `kind: 'soft'` cylinders (block sight, not movement).
* **`log_bridge`** lies along Y, crown (broken) end at −Y, root plate at
  +Y. Walkable chain of 5 boxes along the trunk, tops at the trunk top
  (rising gently from ~0.70 m at the −Y end to ~1.40 m near the root
  plate), plus a solid box for the root plate. Its node extra `walk`
  gives the walkable span `y0..y1` and the top heights at both ends
  (Blender space). Place it across the river so both ends rest on the
  banks.
* **Grass, fern, reeds**: no colliders, ≤ 120 tris, solid closed blades
  (visible from every side, no alpha, no double-sided material needed).
* Materials are palette keys only: `bark_pine`, `bark_oak`, `needles`,
  `leaves`, `deadwood`, `rock`, `rock_dark`, `moss`, `grass`, `reed`, `dirt`.

## What the game must know

* **Origins.** Trees, bushes, stumps and ground cover: origin at the trunk /
  clump centre on the ground (z = 0), so the crown may be a little off
  centre (lean). Hedges: centred, base on the ground. Boulders and the
  outcrop are **partly sunk**: their lowest vertex is below z = 0 (boulders
  ~12 % of their height, outcrop ~0.45 m) so they sit into uneven terrain;
  sizes above include the sunk part.
* **LODs.** `*_lod` nodes share the full node's silhouette and colours and
  have **no colliders** — register colliders from the full node only. Swap
  at ~60–90 m (fog hides the rest).
* **Instancing.** Every tree/grass node is a single mesh with ≤ 2 primitives
  (bark + foliage) — suitable for `InstancedMesh` per primitive. Random yaw
  per instance is fine for everything except `log_bridge` and hedges.
* **Hedges** tile along X every **4.0 m**: the leaf body overhangs each end
  by ~0.3–0.45 m with tapered ends, so neighbours overlap and hide the joint
  (a 180° yaw on alternate segments hides repetition). Collider: one solid
  box (blocks movement, bullets and sight — bocage is impassable);
  `hedge_low` (top 1.15 m) is vaultable.
* **Bushes** use `kind: 'soft'` cylinders (block sight, not movement).
* **`log_bridge`** lies along Y, crown (broken) end at −Y, root plate at
  +Y. Walkable chain of 5 boxes along the trunk, tops at the trunk top
  (rising gently from ~0.70 m at the −Y end to ~1.40 m near the root
  plate), plus a solid box for the root plate. Its node extra `walk`
  gives the walkable span `y0..y1` and the top heights at both ends
  (Blender space). Place it across the river so both ends rest on the
  banks.
* **Grass, fern, reeds**: no colliders, ≤ 120 tris, solid closed blades
  (visible from every side, no alpha, no double-sided material needed).
* Materials are palette keys only: `bark_pine`, `bark_oak`, `needles`,
  `leaves`, `deadwood`, `rock`, `rock_dark`, `moss`, `grass`, `reed`, `dirt`.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/vojta/Library/Application REDACTED

# Built-in browser

The built-in browser is a real browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, separate from the person's Chrome. Its tools are named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*` when the session itself runs inside the desktop app, and `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when the session runs in the cloud (started from the web, a phone, or the desktop app) and is linked to the person's computer. The names after the prefix are the same either way, Claude uses whichever prefix is actually present, and this skill refers to the tools by the part after the prefix.

If the only built-in browser tool present is `enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser`, Claude calls it first: it turns the built-in browser on for this conversation, and the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` tools appear once it has run.

## What the person can see

The browser pane shares the desktop app's side panel with artifacts, documents, and file previews, and the panel shows one of them at a time. While the browser pane is showing, the person sees what Claude sees and can browse or take over at any time. While something else is open in the panel, or the panel is closed, the built-in browser keeps working but the person cannot see it.

Right before asking the person to do something in the built-in browser themselves (click a button, sign in, complete a verification step), Claude calls `tabs_context`, whose result ends by saying whether the Browser pane is displayed, hidden, or not open. If the pane is not open, Claude opens the page first and checks again. If the pane is hidden, Claude first asks the person to bring the browser back in the Claude desktop app: press Cmd+Shift+B on Mac or Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows, or close whatever else is open in the side panel and click the globe icon (the Browser button). Claude then says what to do in the browser. Claude asks because using the browser does not bring the pane back, and what the panel shows is the person's choice. Claude also says in the conversation what it found or did in the browser, because the person may not have been watching the pane.

## Sign-ins persist, and they are the person's

The built-in browser keeps its own persistent profile, shared across the desktop app's sessions. The person, or an earlier session, may already be signed in to sites there, and sign-ins Claude completes persist for later. Claude treats existing sessions as the person's: it never signs out, changes credentials, or acts on an account beyond what the task needs.

## Tabs

The built-in browser has tabs. `preview_start` with a `url` opens an additional tab at that URL in one call and returns a `tabId`, leaving existing tabs untouched, so Claude prefers it over `tabs_create` followed by `navigate` when the destination is already known. `navigate`, `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, `computer`, `form_input`, and the console and network readers act on the tab named by `tabId`; omitting `tabId` targets the active tab, and `tabs_context` lists the open tabs.

## Loading via ToolSearch

Claude loads the built-in browser tools in bulk, not one-by-one: if they are in the deferred list, Claude loads them all in a single ToolSearch call whose query is their full name prefix, for example `{ query: "mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__", max_results: 64 }`.

## Reading pages

Claude prefers `get_page_text` and `read_page` over screenshots for reading, because they return the page's actual text and structure rather than pixels of the visible viewport. `computer` with action "screenshot" is for when the visual layout is the point or the person asks to see the page.

## Site approvals, blocked sites, and request_access

Depending on the person's approval settings, the person may be asked to approve a site before Claude acts on it, and some sites are blocked outright. Claude waits for a pending approval rather than working around it. If a page is refused or an approval is declined, Claude tells the person and moves on rather than retrying.

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, approvals can be answered from any of the person's devices and may take a moment to arrive, and the session may also have a `request_access` tool. If a browser tool answers that the site is not allowed yet and `request_access` is present, Claude calls it with that site's URL and scope "once" (or "site" when the task will keep using that site), waits for the person's answer, and then retries the original tool. Without `request_access`, a refused site is handled as above: Claude tells the person and moves on.

## What the built-in browser cannot open

The built-in browser cannot open `file://` URLs or `localhost` servers that Claude starts itself, because those run where Claude's shell runs, which is not where the browser pane runs. To show the person HTML that Claude generated, Claude uses an artifact instead.

## When the built-in browser cannot be reached

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, the pane runs in the Claude desktop app on the person's computer while Claude runs elsewhere, so it is reachable only while that app is open and online. If those tool calls cannot reach the desktop app (connection errors or no response), Claude tells the person the built-in browser looks offline on their computer rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.
